feedback.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0x+0y+0z \\ 1x+(-1)y+(-1)z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
